# dagsterplus_service_token (Resource)

Manages a Dagster+ service token. The token value is only available at creation time; it cannot be recovered after import. Changing service_user_id forces a new resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "dagsterplus_service_user" "ci_bot" {
  name        = "ci-bot"
  description = "Service user for CI/CD pipelines"
}

resource "dagsterplus_service_token" "ci_token" {
  service_user_id = dagsterplus_service_user.ci_bot.id
  description     = "CI pipeline token"
}

# The token value is only available at creation time
output "ci_token_value" {
  value     = dagsterplus_service_token.ci_token.token
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `service_user_id` (String) The ID of the service user this token belongs to. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `description` (String) An optional description for the token.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The token ID assigned by Dagster+.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The service token value. Only populated on creation; not recoverable after import.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a service token by its server-assigned ID
# Note: the token value cannot be recovered after import — add it to ImportStateVerifyIgnore
# Note: service_user_id must be set manually after import as it is not returned by the API
terraform import dagsterplus_service_token.ci_token <token-id>
```
